### 🐛 Describe the bug ## Description On stock vLLM 0.31.0 (zero local modifications), with a repetitive prompt on a **hybrid linear-attention model** (Qwen3.5-9B: gated-delta-net (GDN) layers + full-attention layers), the **first speculative-verify forward of width ≥ 8 rows that crosses the junction `prompt_len + 8`** makes the request stop after exactly 10 tokens with `finish_reason="stop"`. Greedy sampling produces an **EOS token on the verify forward's row for absolute position `prompt_len + 8`** (the 8th generated position after the prefill boundary) — where greedy *sequential* decode on the identical prefix emits a normal token. This is **not specific to `ngram_gpu` or to a single model runner**. Two independent configurations reproduce it on the same model and the same prompt surface: - `method="ngram_gpu"` with `num_speculative_tokens` **K=7 or K=8** — runs on the V1 (MRV1) runner (on 0.31.0 `ngram_gpu` is on the MRV2 unsupported list, see Environment); - stock `method="mtp"` with `num_speculative_tokens=8` under `VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1` — reproduces on the **Model Runner V2**, byte-identical output text (see "Additional evidence"; K=8 is the only MTP width tested so far). So the binding condition is the **wide verify forward itself on a hybrid GDN model at that junction** — not the draft source (n-gram table vs. neural MTP head) and not the model runner. *Face caveat (2026-10-13):* all width/runner claims in this report are pinned to one fixed prompt spelling — the 1845-token prompt has a 1-token variant on which **plain, non-speculative greedy decode also stops at 10 tokens on both runners**, so only the primary face below (where plain and narrow-verify controls complete normally) can isolate verify width; see "Appendix: prompt-variant sensitivity (why the control matters)". On the ngram surface the threshold is sharp and reproducible: **K ≤ 6 completes normally, K ≥ 7 always early-stops** (measured with `--enforce-eager`) on the same prompt (main face — the spelling in "Reproduction" above; see Appendix for a 1-token prompt variant on which even K=3 and plain decode stop). **Prompt content is part of the trigger, not an incidental:** the complete early stop (10 tokens / `stop`) has been observed only at K ≥ 7 on high-repetition structured-block faces whose wide-verify drafts are near-fully accepted; the same K=8 on a low-acceptance prose face does **not** early-stop, it merely degrades severely (64 generated tokens over 472 drafts with only 5 accepted, finishing `length` — see the "8 + non-repetitive prompt" row of the matrix below). The face content decides whether the near-tie at the junction is actually crossed, so reproduce with the attached prompt verbatim — the repetitive `[DATA]` block spelling above, ending on the block's trailing `\n`; "severe degradation without early stop" on a prose prompt is the expected face-sensitivity, not a refutation of the threshold. ## Environment - vLLM: `0.31.0` wheel (service fingerprint `vllm-0.31.0-13c091b4`; source tree == tag `v0.31.0`, commit `db9527a4`) — **stock, no patches** - Model: Qwen3.5-9B (HF id `Qwen/Qwen3.5-9B`; hybrid: GDN linear-attention layers + full attention; VLM architecture, run text-only via `--language-model-only`). The model ships an MTP head; the primary repro uses `method="ngram_gpu"` only, while the second repro (Additional evidence) uses exactly that MTP head as the draft source on Model Runner V2. - Hardware: NVIDIA RTX 4090 (24 GiB), single GPU, TP=1, PP=1 - torch `2.13.0+cu130`, Python 3.11 (full `collect_env.py` output attached — pasted in the "Your current environment" field; captured on this repro host 2026-10-13) - `--enforce-eager` reproduces → this ≥8-wide repro **does not require** `torch.compile` or CUDA graphs (a pure eager forward is sufficient). No converse claim is made: compiled-kernel artifacts add their own sensitivity at *narrower* verify widths on this same face — see "Additional evidence — the same near-tie is also flipped by the compiled-kernel artifact". - Async scheduling **off** reproduces (and on reproduces the same); all forensics below are from sync-mode runs. - Model runner note: on 0.31.0, `ngram_gpu` is on the Model-Runner-V2 unsupported list (`vllm/config/vllm.py:3073-3083`), so the engine logs `Model Runner V2 does not yet support speculative method 'ngram_gpu'; using the V1 model runner instead.` (`vllm/config/vllm.py:752-757`) and the ngram repro runs **on the V1 (MRV1) model runner**. The forensic captures below instrument that path. The runner dependency was then removed: the identical junction reproduces on the **stock Model Runner V2** with `method="mtp"` (V2-effectiveness attestation in "Additional evidence"), so no whitelist fallback is involved in that arm. ## Reproduction ### 1) Serve-level repro (no code changes required) ```bash vllm serve /path/to/Qwen3.5-9B \ --port 8080 --max-model-len 2048 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.90 \ --tensor-parallel-size 1 --dtype bfloat16 --max-num-seqs 4 \ --max-num-batched-tokens 2048 --enforce-eager --language-model-only \ --speculative-config '{"method":"ngram_gpu","num_speculative_tokens":8,"prompt_lookup_min":5,"prompt_lookup_max":8}' ``` Build the request body (repetitive block ×60 + continuation cue + block ×3 → **1845 prompt tokens** with this model's tokenizer; **use this exact spelling** — a 1-token variant of the same prompt behaves qualitatively differently, see Appendix: prompt-variant sensitivity): ```python import json block = "[DATA] id=42 name=widget price=19.99 region=NA warehouse=W1 qty=137\n" prompt = ("The report template repeats a block.\n" + block * 60 + "\nNow continue the report in the same style:\n" + block * 3) print(json.dumps({"model": "/path/to/Qwen3.5-9B", "prompt": prompt, "max_tokens": 96, "temperature": 0.0})) ``` ```bash python gen.py > body.json curl -s http://127.0.0.1:8080/v1/completions -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -d @body.json ``` Observed response (abridged; fields verbatim, `smoke-ngram8-resp.json`): 10 completion tokens, `finish_reason="stop"`, text truncated mid-block: ```json {"choices":[{"text":"[DATA] id=42 name=","finish_reason":"stop"}], "usage":{"prompt_tokens":1845,"completion_tokens":10,"total_tokens":1855}} ``` `/metrics` confirms a single verification step accepted all 8 drafts (`vllm:spec_decode_num_accepted_tokens_per_pos_total{position=0..7}` each `+1.0`, `BASELINE-2026-10-10.md`), i.e. the first n-gram proposal chain is **perfect**, and the token *after* the accepted chain is EOS. Environment notes: `VLLM_ATTENTION_BACKEND=FLASH_ATTN` and `VLLM_USE_FLASHINFER_SAMPLER=0` were set only to work around unrelated flashinfer-JIT/toolchain issues on this machine; they do not affect acceptance logic. ### 2) In-process repro (also stock-only) Same configuration through `LLM(...)`, one greedy request (`temperature=0.0, max_tokens=96`). The observable assertion is just: **K=7/8 ⇒ `len(output.token_ids) == 10` and last token == `eos_token_id (248046)`; K≤6 ⇒ 96 tokens, `finish='length'`.** ## Reproduction matrix (same prompt, greedy) | K (`num_speculative_tokens`) | method / runner | first verify width (rows) | result | sampled sequence (token ids) | |---|---|---|---|---| | 3 | ngram_gpu / MRV1 | 4 | normal, 96 tok, `length` | (accepts 69/78 drafts, baseline) | | 4 | ngram_gpu / MRV1 | 5 | normal, `length` | (accepts 159/172 drafts, baseline) | | 6 | ngram_gpu / MRV1 | 7 | **normal**, 96 tok, `length` | `58,17247,60,850,28,19,17,803,28,17247,60,…` (runs to 96) | | 7 | ngram_gpu / MRV1 | 8 | **early stop: 10 tok, `stop`** | `58,17247,60,850,28,19,17,803,28,248046(EOS)` | | 8 | ngram_gpu / MRV1 | 9 | **early stop: 10 tok, `stop`** | `58,17247,60,850,28,19,17,803,28,248046(EOS)` | | 8 + non-repetitive prompt | ngram_gpu / MRV1 | ≤9 | normal, 64 tok, `length` | acceptance 5/472 (drafts rejected; **no early stop**) | | 8 | mtp / **stock MRV2** (`VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1`) | 9 | **early stop: 10 tok, `stop`** (independently on both a `max_tokens=24` and a `max_tokens=96` request) | output text `'[DATA] id=42 name='` byte-identical to the ngram K=7/8 rows; `a3-{r1-mt24,r2-mt96}-resp.json` | (K=3/4/K=8-prose rows from `BASELINE-2026-10-10.md`; K=6/7/8 ngram rows from the sync in-process forensics below; V2-MTP row from the `a3-*` archive entries raw captures — see "Additional evidence". The K≤6-normal / K≥7-early-stop threshold and the prose-prompt control are established on the ngram surface; on the MTP@MRV2 surface only K=8 has been tested so far. The ngram rows all use the primary (with-blank-line) prompt spelling above; the V2-MTP row used the 1-token no-blank-line variant of the same 1845-token surface — the early-stop repro stands on that face, but on that face even plain decode stops, so width isolation comes only from the ngram rows (see Appendix: prompt-variant sensitivity).) ## Observed vs Expected - **Expected:** K=8 behaves like K=6 on this prompt: the repetitive n-gram chain is accepted and the continuation proceeds (`finish=length` at `max_tokens`). Greedy sequential decode at the failing position emits `17247` ("DATA"), never EOS. - **Observed:** with verify width ≥ 8, the logit row whose input position is `prompt_len+8` (=1853 here; `prompt_len=1845`) has **argmax = EOS `248046`**; after all 8 drafts are accepted, that EOS terminates the request. Silent — no error, `finish_reason="stop"`. - EOS (`248046`) ≠ pad (`248044`) for this tokenizer, so this is not a pad-token leak. ## Relationship to prior reports We searched the issue tracker thoroughly; we found reports sharing the *configuration* (hybrid GDN + spec decode, sometimes + prefix caching) but none with this *symptom class* — a byte-clean completion that dies in a **single EOS sampling decision at a fixed near-tied position**. The closest, and why we believe this is distinct (deferring to maintainer judgment): - **#39273** (open) — *"Ngram speculative decoding produces corrupted output on hybrid GDN (Qwen3.5) models"* (reported on v0.18.1, later datapoints on v0.26.x). Same model family and draft method, different symptom: there the output progressively **degenerates into repeated / truncated fragments**, consistent with that thread's state-rollback hypothesis. Here the output is byte-correct up to a clean 1-token early stop (`[DATA] id=42 name=` + EOS), the acceptance/state ledger is verified self-consistent step-by-step in the captures (L1; first root-cause bullet below), and the failure is a per-position numerics flip, not a state desync. (The initial report there scoped MTP out; later comments extend the corruption class toward MTP on other model versions — our MTP@V2 arm is still a different symptom.) - **#53912 / #43559** — prefix caching + MTP corrupting output on hybrid GDN/Mamba models (v0.28.0 / v0.26.x). Same configuration pair, different symptom: low-entropy **garbage** (repeated punctuation, empty output, semantic corruption), not early stop. That failure class has a merged fix series — **#45100** (async accepted-count race), **#51113** (mamba-align prefill chunk alignment), **#50729** (overlapping state-copy race, shipped in v0.28.1) — all of which predate the v0.31.0 this report reproduces on. - **#45100** in particular cannot be the mechanism here. Its failure signature does include a fast end with EOS — but always *with* prompt-memory loss / garbled text (this report's output is byte-clean up to the single EOS), it is an async-scheduling-only race, and it was merged in June 2026 — **over three months before the v0.31.0 this repro runs on**, i.e. every capture here already contains that fix. - **Post-release main merges we are aware of** (all landed *after* the v0.31.0 tag; this report targets the latest stable release, v0.31.0): **#56531** (routes speculation-capable rows consistently through the speculative path, fixing #40875's path-switch stale-state corruption) and **#55504** (bounds oversized query widths out of GDN's bounded speculative state layout) address corruption mechanisms in that family; our captures show the acceptance/state ledger already self-consistent on this repro (L1 + the root-cause bullets), so we do not expect either to cover this junction flip — happy to retest on current main on request. Separately, **#40704** has since added an `ngram_gpu` speculator for Model Runner V2 on main; our runner-independence finding was obtained pre-merge (V1 arm via the 0.31.0 whitelist fallback, V2 arm via stock `mtp`) and is exactly the property #40704 now makes trivially testable upstream. The per-position logit captures below let triage verify this separation mechanically: an acceptance/state-rollback bug cannot produce "all verify rows correct except one fixed position, only at ≥8-slot verify, only with chunked prefill, on a one-token-tied prompt face". ## Evidence chain (4 layers, all from instrumented stock runs) All artifacts below are from `--enforce-eager`, `async_scheduling=False` runs; excerpts from the attached files. **L1 — the verify input pipeline is correct** (rules out table corruption / `-1` leak / position mislabel). `t2-forensic2-k8-sync-steps.jsonl`, the failing verify forward (EXCERPT): ```json {"event": "config", "K": 8, "spec": {"method": "ngram_gpu", "num_speculative_tokens": 8, "prompt_lookup_min": 5, "prompt_lookup_max": 8}, "eos_id": 248046, "pad_id": 248044, "async_scheduling": false, "prompt_len": 1845} {"event": "model_forward", "step": 2, "n_in": 9, "input_ids": [58, 17247, 60, 850, 28, 19, 17, 803, 28], "positions": [[1845,1846,1847,1848,1849,1850,1851,1852,1853], x3]} # 3x = mrope stacked rows {"event": "compute_logits", "step": 4, "n_rows": 9, "argmax": [17247, 60, 850, 28, 19, 17, 803, 28, 248046]} ``` 9 input rows = 1 sampled token + 8 drafts; **no `-1`, no pad tokens, positions contiguous 1845..1853**; the n-gram kernel reported 8 valid drafts (`n_valid=8`, recorded in `t2-forensic-k8-sync-steps.jsonl`), and the 8 draft rows' argmax exactly reproduce the drafts (all accepted). Row 8 = the **target row** (predicts the token at position 1854) → EOS. Sync-mode scheduler-side trimming shows no `-1` leakage (same file: trim 8→8, neg1 0→0). **L2 — the model's own per-row logits say EOS at that row** (same capture as L1; `compute_logits` is hooked right after the target LM head, so this is the model output, not a sampling artifact). **L3 — the same position computes normally under other widths / sequential decode.** - K=7, first verify (8 wide, positions 1845..1852): all 8 rows correct — `argmax [17247,60,850,28,19,17,803,28]`; 7/7 accepted, bonus `28` lands at position 1853. Second verify (8 wide, positions **1853**..1860): **row 0 argmax = `248046` (EOS)** → stop. (`t2-forensic2-k7-sync-steps.jsonl`) - K=6, second verify (7 wide, positions 1852..1858): **row 1 (input position 1853) argmax = `17247`** — matching greedy sequential decode at the identical prefix; the scheduled draft `9505` is rejected, the request survives and completes 96 tokens; every later 7-wide verify (covering 1853 and all positions beyond) stays correct. (`t2-forensic2-k6-sync-steps.jsonl`) - No-spec greedy control (K=0): emits `…28, 17247, 60, …` at the junction and finishes `length` — EOS never appears. (`t2-forensic-nospec-steps.jsonl`) - K=8 with a *non-repetitive* prompt: acceptance collapses (drafts rejected, no 8-deep acceptance chain) but **no early stop** — the EOS row only fires when the wide verify forward actually runs on this workload. The failing row is bound to **absolute position 1853 = prompt_len + 8**, not to its row index (K=8: row 8; K=7: row 0) and not to the step index (K=7 fails on its *second* verify). **L4 — an independent forward (transformers reference implementation of the same weights, incl. reference GDN) sees a near-tie at this position, EOS in second place.** From `t2-probe-logits.out` (EXCERPT; context = prompt + `[58]` + the 8 draft tokens = exactly the verify step's prefix, prediction at position 1854): ```text [A] prompt+[58]+8drafts n_in=1854 -> argmax=17247 top5=[(17247, 17.25), (248046, 15.75), (498, 14.4375), (19, 14.4375), (271, 13.875)] [C] prompt+[58] n_in=1846 -> argmax=17247 (logit 23.625) [D] prompt n_in=1845 -> argmax=58 (logit 22.25) ``` So at the identical prefix: reference forward → `17247` ("DATA") with **EOS second, Δlogit ≈ 1.5 in bf16**; vLLM sequential → `17247`; vLLM **verify** forward (≥8 rows) → **EOS**. This is a genuinely near-degenerate point, which is consistent with a small state/numerics difference flipping the argmax, and inconsistent with corrupted inputs (L1). ## Additional evidence — same junction on the stock Model Runner V2 with MTP drafts (2026-10-13) To test whether the failure depends on the n-gram proposer or on the V1 runner (it cannot run on V2 directly — `ngram_gpu` is whitelist-blocked there), we served the **same model** with **`method="mtp"`, `num_speculative_tokens=8`** and `VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1`, and sent the **same 1845-token repetitive prompt surface** (same model, same junction — only the draft source, the model runner, and (by one token) the prompt spelling changed; note this arm's driver spells the prompt in the *no-blank-line* 1-token variant, both spellings tokenize to exactly 1845 tokens — see Appendix: prompt-variant sensitivity), greedy, twice. The picture is **one shared numerical path (the hybrid model's GDN / linear-attention kernels) crossed by three orthogonal configuration knobs (verify width, compiled-kernel bundle, prefill chunking)**. The model runner is *not* one of the knobs — see the bit-level bullet below. Full report and raw captures are in the the `t6` / `e1-table-*` archive entries attachment block of the manifest. - **The shared path: three mathematically equivalent GDN kernels with different numerics.** In this model family the GDN layers execute the same recurrence through a *different kernel per step shape*: - 1-row decode: Triton packed-recurrent kernel (`fused_recurrent_gated_delta_rule_packed_decode`, on by default via `VLLM_ENABLE_FLA_PACKED_RECURRENT_DECODE`); - spec verify whose per-request state-slot count `K + 1` (`num_speculative_tokens = K`) fits `MAX_FUSED_GDN_MTP_TOKENS = 8`: CUDA fused decode-MTP kernel (`torch.ops._C.fused_gdn_decode_post_conv_mtp`); - spec verify at `K + 1 = 9` (K = 8): the Triton `fused_sigmoid_gating_delta_rule_update_kernel` spec-decoding branch. The three kernels agree mathematically but differ in fp32 reduction order (warp-pair tree vs. tiled `tl.sum` tree vs. single-slot packed), fast-math gates, and conv sliding. At the L4 near-tie these path differences are not tiny: at position 1853 they measure Δlogit("DATA" 17247) = **−2.4375** (the 8-row CUDA-fused verify row) and **−1.5625** (the 9-row Triton row, with Δlogit(EOS) = +0.1875) against the sequential decode's margin of +1.5625 — deterministic crossings — while every other position 1845–1852 moves ≤ 1.25 logits on the same arm pair and no argmax changes (`e1-table-flip-vs-seqapc.txt`, `e1-table-spec8v1-vs-seqv1.txt`, `e1-table-v2-clean.txt`). The pathology is not "wide verify is wrong everywhere" — it is "wide verify flips *this* coin". - **The K ≥ 7 threshold is a kernel-branch boundary; the "8-related chunking in the GDN state path" is found — and it is not a bookkeeping defect.** The state-slot / `num_accepted` ledger checks out self-consistent in every capture (first-verify snapshot `n_acc = [1]`, slot table `[1, K+1]`, `spec_cu = [0, 9]` at K=8; the K=6 row at position 1853 carries exactly the same value as sequential decode): **no violation was found** on either the MRV1 `_update_states_after_model_execute` → `postprocess_mamba_align_gpu` path or the MRV2 `MambaHybridModelState.postprocess_state` path. Our earlier first hypothesis — hybrid spec-decode state *misalignment* at ≥8-row verify — is therefore ruled out on this repro, and the then-alternative (numerical drift between equivalent paths) is the primary mechanism. The flip onset coincides with the verify step reaching the `MAX_FUSED_GDN_MTP_TOKENS = 8` state-slot capacity line: the junction margin (verify vs. sequential reference) reads **+0.625 at 7 slots (K=6, clean), −1.625 at 8 slots (K=7), −0.1875 at 9 slots (K=8, Triton side)** — the coupling of that branch line with the near-tie's sign, not a state desync. - **The divergence is seeded in layer 0 of the verify forward.** With bit-identical bf16 inputs into layer 0 (the first GDN layer), its output already differs by 9.4e-5 relative between verify and sequential decode at the same fed position — attributable only to the GDN core itself (one 9-token scan vs. nine single-step recursions). The difference enters the bf16 grid at layer 2 (6e-3) and grows monotonically across the 32 layers (full-attention layers mix and amplify, never re-seed; relative peak 5.6e-2) into the O(1) logit flip at the junction (`e1-table-layers-1853.txt`). This is consistent with the dense (non-hybrid) control in "What we ruled out" item 5 staying clean at isomorphic shapes: no GDN kernel layer exists on that path. - **Runner independence upgraded from "same verdict" to bit-level.** Both model runners feed `num_accepted_tokens` into the **same** `GDNAttentionMetadataBuilder` and execute the **same** GDN attention layer class; at the junction their verify rows are not merely similar — they are **bit-identical** logits (`spec8_apc_v1.jsonl` vs. `spec8_apc_v2.jsonl`), and the full per-position difference tables coincide value-for-value at the non-flipping widths. The shared substrate beneath the two *independently implemented* postprocesses is the kernel layer, not a common bookkeeping invariant. (Provenance: the V2 `ngram_gpu` captures in this pair required a minimal local enablement patch — stock 0.31.0's whitelist blocks `ngram_gpu` on V2 — while the width-2 `method="mtp"` pairs cited alongside (`mtp1_apc_v1_eager` vs `mtp1_apc_v2_eager`, and the compiled pair, likewise both flipping) run stock `method="mtp"` paths on both runners; the bit-identity conclusion holds on either pair.) - **Knob (new): prefill chunking via `enable_prefix_caching`.** The repro above silently relies on the 0.31.0 default `enable_prefix_caching=True`, which makes the 1845-token prefill execute in **two chunks (1680 + 165)**; the recurrent state propagated from the chunk boundary is part of what gives the interaction term its flipping sign at 1853. With `enable_prefix_caching=False` explicitly set (single-segment prefill), **every tested width — plain decode and K ∈ {6, 7, 8} (verify widths 7/8/9) — is clean on both runners** (`e1-table-spec8v1-vs-seqv1.txt`, `e1-table-flip-vs-cleantier.txt`, `e1-table-v2-clean.txt`). Disabling prefix caching is therefore a **mask, not a fix** — it moves this position's interaction term off the flipping sign, while the tie itself stays reachable (the next bullet flips it at width 1) — but it is a hard reproducibility condition: **reproducers must keep/pin `enable_prefix_caching=True`** (see the Configuration section). - **Knob (the second, already demonstrated above — now shown to reach even plain decode): the compiled numerical bundle.** The compiled-kernel artifact section above tested plain controls only with CUDA graphs *on*. In a further compiled configuration — `VLLM_COMPILE` with `cudagraph_mode=NONE`, zero captures — the same position flips at width 2 on **both** runners (MTP K=1, junction gaps −0.375 and −0.25) *and* under **plain width-1 greedy decode with no speculative verify involved at all** (EOS logit 16.625 — bit-equal to the width-2 compiled arms' EOS value — top-1 over "DATA" 15.375; `seq_apc_v2_comp.jsonl`), while the eager bundle keeps both runners clean and bit-identical at widths 1–2 (gap +0.375; `mtp1_apc_v1_eager.jsonl`, `mtp1_apc_v2_eager.jsonl`). Read honestly: **this face's position 1853 is a globally ill-conditioned tie on this model** — any reordering of numerically equivalent kernel paths can land it on EOS — and speculative verify width is the knob that reaches it *without leaving the default configuration*. - **The binding is content, not a `prompt_len+8` coordinate rule.** The same face constructed eight tokens shorter (1837-token prompt, default prefix caching) completes normally on the primary K=8 wide-verify recipe — both of its verify steps, the second of which crosses the original absolute 1853 mid-stream, stay clean. The near-tied content moves with the prompt and the wide-verify steps no longer light it; the L3 controls likewise show that verifies which merely *cross* the junction mid-stream (after a partial acceptance) stay clean. So "the 8th slot past the prefill boundary" was a coincidence of this fixed spelling × fixed K, not an engine coordinate rule. What binds is the conjunction: **near-tie content at absolute position 1853 × chunked-prefill state × ≥8-slot verify branch** — remove any factor and the coin does not flip (`T6-GDN-ROOTCAUSE.md` §2.3, §5.1). **Why this remains a spec-decode bug even though other knobs can flip the same coin.** The preceding bullets invite the objection "plain decode can also be made to flip here, so this is model numerics, not a spec-decode defect". Two independent answers, both load-bearing for this report: 1. **Only the spec-verify knob fires inside the default configuration.** Under `--enforce-eager` (no `torch.compile`, no CUDA graphs) with everything else at engine defaults — prefix caching included — plain sequential decode completes this prompt normally (96 tokens, `length`) and so does every verify narrower than 8 rows; the *only* configuration change that switches on the silent truncation is `num_speculative_tokens ≥ 7`. Users hit this by raising one draft-length number, with no exotic flags; the compiled-bundle arms, by contrast, require leaving that minimal configuration. 2. **The verify path changes what a flipped bit *means*.** Sequential decode that sampled EOS at this position would simply end a request that was ending anyway. In the wide-verify step, the EOS is produced by a row **no sequential path ever evaluates alone**, is committed right after an 8/8-perfect draft acceptance, and the acceptance/rollback semantics convert that single ulp-scale numerical event into a **silently truncated completion** — 10 of 96 requested tokens, `finish_reason="stop"`, no error. The tie's conditioning decides the coin; the spec-decode machinery decides the damage, through its own semantics. Fix candidates therefore legitimately sit on the spec-decode side (verify-vs-decode decision consistency at near-ties, e.g. acceptance behavior insensitive to ulp-scale path noise) as well as on the GDN side (numerical consistency among the three kernels, behavior at the 8-slot branch line) — we are glad to test either. The consequence is severe (silent truncation, wrong `finish_reason`), and the trigger is configuration-level (`num_speculative_tokens ≥ 7`), not adversarial. ## Additional notes - Reproduction is deterministic across serve/in-process, sync/async scheduling, eager mode, and repeated runs on three different dates (2026-10-10 serve smoke, 2026-10-12 in-process forensics, 2026-10-13 V2/MTP serve re-runs — all 10 tokens, same text, same EOS). - **Both model runners are affected, and they implement the hybrid spec-decode state postprocess independently** (MRV1: `_update_states_after_model_execute` → `postprocess_mamba_align_gpu` in `gpu_model_runner.py`/`mamba_utils.py`; MRV2: `MambaHybridModelState.postprocess_state` in `v1/worker/gpu/model_states/mamba_hybrid.py` — a separate code path that documents itself as *mirroring* the V1 align postprocess, not shared code).
